newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says paid cereals farmers 8.5 bn Ecus too much.
newsitem.headline: EU says paid cereals farmers 8.5 bn Ecus too much.

text.p: European Union cereals farmers, excluding durum wheat producers, were over-paid by 8.46 billion Ecus during the past four seasons, the European Commission said on Friday.
The estimate was contained in a working document, obtained by Reuters, which examined a British study in April putting over-compensation for cereals farmers at 14.3 billion Ecus.
The figures rise to 9.67 billion and 19.7 billion Ecus respectively if aid for durum wheat producers is included.
The payments were agreed by EU farm ministers in 1992 to compensate farmers for a 30 percent reduction in intervention prices as part of reforms to reduce grain surpluses.
But since then market prices have mostly been well above intervention levels and cereals farmers have been paid for losses they never suffered.
Compensatory aid was fixed at 45 Ecus a tonne, corresponding to an expected market price five percent above the intervention level of 100 Ecus a tonne.
Over-compensation was put at 510 million Ecus in 1993/94, rising to 2.10 billion in 1994/95 and peaking at 3.94 billion in 1995/96, before falling to 2.00 billion in 1996/97.
This has prompted Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler to propose a 1.4 billion Ecu cut in aid to cereals farmers to help beef farmers hit by the mad cow crisis.
The proposal, which is opposed by nearly all member states, will be discussed by farm ministers in Luxembourg from June 23-25 along with the 1997/98 (July/June) farm price package.
They argue that the cuts are not needed because of an estimated one billion Ecu underspend in the 1997 budget.
